extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent applicants/attorneys prosecuting applications
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and substantive standards for making, traversing, electing, and rejoinder of restriction requirements in patent applications under 35 U.S.C. 111, including form-paragraph usage and effects on prosecution rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper grounds for a restriction requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction is proper where the inventions are independent or distinct and where there would be a serious burden on the examiner if restriction is not required because the inventions require a different field of search (see MPEP § 808.02).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If inventions are independent/distinct and searches would be unduly burdensome or in different fields, restriction may be required; the examiner should cite MPEP § 808.02 when asserting this ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include inventorship-correction paragraph for joint inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 8.23.02 must be included in all restriction requirements for applications having joint inventors reminding applicant to correct inventorship if claims to a non-elected invention are canceled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises that correction under 37 CFR 1.48(a) must be accompanied by an application data sheet per 37 CFR 1.76 and the processing fee under 37 CFR 1.17(i). Must be included in restriction requirements for joint-inventor applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election and reply obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Election is the designation of the particular one of two or more disclosed inventions that will be prosecuted. A reply should be made to each point raised by the examiner and may include a traverse or compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must make an election; examiner will not make it for the applicant. Replies should address each point in the examiner’s action and may accompany a traverse (a statement of reasons the requirement is in error). See 37 CFR 1.111.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traverse must be specific and complete (37 CFR 1.111 / 1.143)
rubrics_metrics.description: A traverse must be a complete statement of the reasons upon which the applicant relies for the conclusion that the restriction requirement is in error and must distinctly and specifically point out supposed errors in the examiner’s action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mere broad allegations are insufficient; reply must reply to every ground of objection and rejection and appear to be a bona fide attempt to advance the application to final action. If not specific, the election will be treated as without traverse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election becomes fixed upon action on claims (818.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Election is fixed when the claims in an application have received an action on their merits by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once the Office has acted on the originally presented claims on the merits, that invention is considered constructively elected for prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election by originally presented claims (818.02(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims originally presented and acted upon by the Office on their merits determine the invention elected by an applicant in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where claims to another invention are properly added and entered before an action, they are treated as original claims for restriction purposes; but generally original acted-upon claims fix the elected invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may require election of species when only generic claims were first prosecuted (818.02(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where only generic claims are first presented and prosecuted and species claims to more than one patentably distinct species are later presented, the examiner may require applicant to elect a single species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This practice addresses unduly extensive and burdensome searches; see MPEP § 808.01(a) for guidance on requiring species election.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election by optional cancellation of claims (818.02(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant cancels claims to all but one invention and the remaining claims are acted upon by the examiner, the invention thus acted upon is elected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cancellation of claims resulting in a single invention acted on by the Office constitutes election of that invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional election required when requesting reconsideration (818.03)
rubrics_metrics.description: When requesting reconsideration or withdrawal/modification of a restriction requirement, the applicant must indicate a provisional election of one invention for prosecution; that invention will be elected if the requirement becomes final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional election allows the Office to reconsider the requirement; if the requirement is repeated and made final, the examiner will act on claims to the invention elected provisionally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant must elect even when traversing (818.03(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional election must be made even though the requirement is traversed; failure to include a provisional election converts the reply to an election without traverse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All restriction requirements should include form paragraph 8.22 advising the need for election and identification of elected claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 8.22: required content for replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies must include (i) an election of a species or invention to be examined and (ii) identification of the claims encompassing the elected invention. To reserve a right to petition, the election must be made with traverse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reply does not distinctly and specifically point out supposed errors, the election is treated as without traverse. If traversing on non-patentable-distinctness grounds, applicant should submit evidence or admit obvious-variant status now on the record; that evidence/admission may be used against the other invention under 35 U.S.C. 103(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Must traverse to preserve right of petition (37 CFR 1.144)
rubrics_metrics.description: To preserve the right to petition the Director from a restriction requirement, applicant must request reconsideration and traverse; petition will not be considered if reconsideration of the requirement was not requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition may be deferred until after final action or allowance of elected claims but must be filed not later than appeal. See 37 CFR 1.144 and MPEP § 818.03(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incomplete or non-specific traverse results in election without traverse
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant does not distinctly and specifically point out supposed errors in the restriction requirement, the election will be treated as an election without traverse (MPEP § 818.03(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 8.25.02 is used to notify applicant that their election is treated as without traverse; this affects petition rights and treatment of nonelected claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traverse involving linking claims (818.03(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: An election combined with a traverse solely of the nonallowance of linking claims is an agreement that restriction is proper if the linking claim is not allowable and improper if it is allowable; if the linking claim is allowed, the requirement must be withdrawn and linked inventions acted on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If traverse asserts other relationships preventing restriction, the merits are contested and petition rights are preserved even if linking claims are canceled; when restriction is contingent on linking claim nonallowability, applicant may petition under 37 CFR 1.144 without waiting for final action on linking claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office generally does not permit shifting elected inventions after action (819)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office's general policy is not to permit the applicant to shift to claiming another invention after an election is made and action given on the elected subject matter; an RCE cannot be used as a matter of right to switch inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A CPA filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d) that is a continuation of its parent and not a divisional carries over an express election from the parent unless otherwise indicated. Where a genus claim is allowable, applicant may prosecute a reasonable number of additional species (37 CFR 1.141).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment and notification for claims held to be drawn to nonelected inventions (37 CFR 1.142(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: All claims that the examiner holds as not being directed to the elected subject matter are withdrawn from further consideration; the examiner should clearly set forth reasons why the claims withdrawn are not readable on the elected invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may traverse the requirement pursuant to 37 CFR 1.143; if a final requirement for restriction is made, applicant may petition under 37 CFR 1.144.

rubrics_metrics.name: After election with traverse: reconsideration, finality, and form-paragraph use (821.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the initial requirement is traversed, it should be reconsidered; if the examiner still finds restriction proper it should be repeated and made final with reply to the traverse. Form paragraph 8.25 should be used to make the restriction requirement final; if withdrawn, specify which groups rejoined and act on the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requirement is repeated and made final, in that and subsequent actions the nonelected claims should be treated using form paragraph 8.05 (Claims Stand Withdrawn With Traverse).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply to final action must cancel non-elected claims or take other action (8.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete reply to a final rejection must include cancellation of nonelected claims or other appropriate action (37 CFR 1.144). Failure to do so will be treated as authorization to cancel the noted claims by examiner’s amendment and pass the case to issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One month or thirty days (whichever is longer) is given to supply omission/correction to avoid abandonment; extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) will not be permitted in this context. Petition under 37 CFR 1.144 must be filed not later than appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of election without traverse (821.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the initial requirement is not traversed, if adhered to, appropriate action should be given on the elected claims; form paragraphs 8.25.01 or 8.25.02 should acknowledge election without traverse. Claims to the nonelected invention should be treated with form paragraph 8.06 (Claims Stand Withdrawn Without Traverse).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Election without traverse shows applicant has not retained the right to petition under 37 CFR 1.144. When the application is otherwise ready for allowance, nonelected claims (except certain species eligible for rejoinder) may be canceled by examiner’s amendment and the application passed to issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims for a different invention added after an Office action (37 CFR 1.145) (821.03)
rubrics_metrics.description: If after an office action, applicant presents claims directed to an invention distinct from and independent of the invention previously claimed, the applicant will be required to restrict to the invention previously claimed if the amendment is entered, subject to reconsideration and review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 8.04 (Election by Original Presentation) to explain why newly submitted claim is directed to a non-elected invention. An amendment canceling all elected claims and presenting only non-elected claims is nonresponsive (use form paragraph 8.26) and applicant is given time to correct (one month/30 days).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejoinder eligibility and requirements (821.04)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for rejoinder, a claim to a nonelected invention must depend from or otherwise require all the limitations of an allowable claim. Rejoined claims must be fully examined for patentability in accordance with 37 CFR 1.104 and must meet 35 U.S.C. 101, 102, 103 and 112.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejoinder withdraws the restriction between the inventions and allows examination on merits of previously nonelected inventions. Applicant should amend nonelected claims during prosecution to require limitations of the elected invention to retain right to rejoinder. Double patenting and 35 U.S.C. 121 considerations apply as explained (e.g., withdrawals may eliminate 35 U.S.C. 121 protection). Consult relevant MPEP sections for biotechnological processes and special process-claim treatments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejoinder between product and process (and product/process-specific rules) (821.04(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where restriction was required between independent or distinct products or processes and all claims to an elected invention are allowable, any restriction between the elected invention and a nonelected invention that depends from or otherwise requires all limitations of an allowable claim should be withdrawn and the previously withdrawn claims rejoined and fully examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims that do not require all limitations remain withdrawn. Amendments presenting additional claims that depend from or require all limitations of an allowable claim will be entered as a matter of right if presented prior to final rejection or allowance. Amendments after final are governed by 37 CFR 1.116; after allowance by 37 CFR 1.312. Use form paragraphs 8.45, 8.49, 8.50, etc., as applicable to notify applicant of rejoin/withdrawal status and double-patenting cautions.
